title: Multiwalled Carbon Nanotubes in Synergy with Glycine-Betaine Improve the Germination of Zea mays and Mitigate the Negative Effects Caused by Water Stress
content: Multiwalled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs) are graphene-based materials with cylindrical structures and exceptional mechanical, electrical, and thermal properties. They have demonstrated potential in enhancing the growth and development of Zea mays by promoting seed germination, improving nutrient uptake, and contributing to overall plant establishment. Furthermore, MWCNTs have been reported to enhance plant tolerance to water deficit conditions, underscoring their role in mitigating abiotic stress [1, 2].
